FUMIGATE

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
FUMIGATION DISASTER:

Interviews
Durban
Zoe Molver – Mother
Luke Molver – Brother
Mntu Mbhele – Investigator
Moses Chetty - Vice-President of the Pest Control Federation of South Africa
Doorstop
HENCHEM – company that sold the substance to Mr I Khan
Irshaad Khan – where is he?

Port Elizabeth - Zoom
Dr Gerrit Verdoon – Poison Specialist

Story
On the evening of Tuesday 27 November 2022, Matri and Nicholas Molver were at home at the their flat in Observatory court, Durban. Unit 31. This was a family flat, that his mother Zoe had been born in, and was a part of the family's lives. The couple had a glass of wine each, Matri was working in her studio on graphic design work for her job at Mr Price Home, and Nick was busy reading a report for his job at an NGO. They showered, and went to bed, never to wake up again.
The next morning, Wednesday 28, their helper couldn’t get in, and told the building’s caretaker Thelma Hall. She knows Luke, Nick’s older brother also lives in the building at number 4. Luke got the spare key, and went upstairs Nick and Matri’s flat… on the way, he smelled a strong chemical smell. He opened the door, and the smell was very strong. He went to the bedroom, and discovered Matri and Nick asleep. Blue and dead. He knew they were already in rigor, and quietly put the covers over them and ran out to call an ambulance.
Zoe was at home when she got a call from the caretaker to come quickly, and that something had happened, she could hear both her other sons – Luke and Matthew howling the background. A strong woman, she arrived calmly. The building had been cordoned off, the bomb squad had been called, the cops from the Berea were there, the fire and rescue services and forensics. People were saying there was poison, and that someone had died. As she made her way up to the flat – she knew. The flat she had grown up in, the flat where her grandfather had passed away silently in his sleep from old age, the flat she had passed down to her son Nicholas after his marriage to Matri 4 years prior… that flat was now a crime scene.

This is what we know now:
On Tuesday afternoon, at the flat next door, number 32, owner Raeesa Kharwa wanted to prepare the empty flat for occupation. She paid a man called Irshaad Khan, who claimed to have a fumigation company, and had placed an advert on Whatsapp to treat borer infestations. When Mr Khan arrived at Observatory Court, the caretaker didn’t know why they were there, but they said they were there to deliver a stove to the unit. There was no mention on any fumigation. She let them in. A little while later they said they were done “spraying,” she asked them what he meant and he said they were spraying for termites. The caretaker asked if she should warn the tenants next door, and he said no. But she was nearby number 35 and decided to anyway. A doctor lived there with his family, and he was home. The doctor asked if he should open their windows, and Mr Khan said yes. But as Matri and Nick weren’t home, they were never warned.
Mr Khan had used aluminum phosphide – which reacts with moisture to become the lethal phosphine gas. This was illegal. This is not a substance that is allowed in urban areas, and is typically used in the killing of rats in grain silo’s. Outside with no one around. That night, Matri and Nick shut all their windows as they had an air conditioner. As it is a heavy gas and there was no airflow, they would have succumbed quickly suffocating in their sleep.
Following further digging into Mr Khan, according to his invoice, which we have, he charged R10,000. This substance is reasonably inexpensive.So he made a massive profit. His company KZN fumigators has two directors, but the other director said he had no idea Irshaad was “active” as they are not registered yet neither as a fumigation company, nor as fumigators. You need both to be able to legally do fumigation according to DAFF.

After
No one was able to find Mr Khan – he disappeared, but now we know where he is. A colleague of Zoe Molver has his address and where he is now. Which we have. We also know that there are two investigations open: one with the saps – who have no arrested anyone yet because the body’s which are at Phoenix Mortuary need to have organ samples taken in order to prove it was the toxin that killed two healthy 30 year olds. Then there is the DAFF investigation: who will follow the powder. How did Khan get it and who sold it to him They took three samples of the powder and will them test it to confirm it is aluminum phosphide – but this was already stated on the invoice from Mr Khan.
In order to secure a conviction and charge Mr Khan, saps needed to take samples of the powder, but they didn’t. This can hopefully be rectified as it is now January and no one has entered the flat since. They could also apply to use DAFFs tests one they come back positive. SAPs have done little to no work so far, however they need to just match the powder to the autopsy toxicology – and they could charge them. However, Zoe has been told that this might take 10 years to get the results back from the state lab because of the backlogs. Obviously they would like to hold Mr Khan responsible for culpable homicide, and I in speaking to experts they can also hold the apartment owner responsible for not checking that they were a legal fumigation entity. The owner has lawyered up.
LAW: Spokesperson for the eThekwini Municipality Msawakhe Mayisela added that fumigation is governed by The Fertilizers, Farm Feeds, Seeds and Remedies Act 36 of 1947.
“Permission does not have to be given by the municipality to fumigate any private premises. However, it is incumbent upon the owner of the property and the Body Corp to ensure the company engaged to do the fumigation is compliant with the appropriate registration in terms of Act 36 of 1947 which governs the approval of pesticides that can be used, the processes for applying, and training requirements for the person applying the pesticide. Further to this, the company must comply with the municipality’s schedule trade by-laws in terms of registration,” said Mayisela.

Besides the fact that SAPS may not be able to get toxicology results soon, they could also go ahead with just the invoice and eyewitnesses, and arrest Khan. They may still get a conviction, since he says he used the substance on the invoice.
The family have hired a PI Captain Mntu Mbhele, regional director of AFIS KZN ( Analytical Forensic Investigation Services), recently retired member of the Hawks.

There is another layer to all of this:
Following the powder, which I have done. Enter Dr Gerhard Verdoorn, which coincidentally the family have also been in contact with. He is from CropLife, and DAFF are highly dependent on his expertise in the area of poisons. He said Mr Khan was not registered as a pest control operator, nor was his company – and in addition to culpable homicide he can be charged with fraud amongst other things. Croplife are an agricultural association and represent 90% of the farming industry. This is a highly flammable substance as well – and a small spark would have set off a “bomb” in that apartment. Meaning Mr Khan put everyone’s lives at risk. Verdoorn says in order for members of the public to protect themselves they need to ask the particular individual or company to produce a registration certificate as a pest control operator from the Department of Agriculture. The certificate needs to specify it's a fumigation certificate.
To validate the credibility of a pest control company and its operators, consult Sapca’s website for a list of companies which adhere to standard operating procedures and follow the pest control operator regulations. Products containing aluminium phosphide are being widely sold in hardware stores, spaza shops and plant nurseries without any legislated safety protocols in place.
“They have to be kept under lock and key — handed over to customers on request, after the necessary verification and interrogation has taken place,” Verdoorn said.
The product is not registered for use as a treatment for borer beetles inside a home, he said, and the amount of tablets used was “complete overkill”.
The flat's doors and windows hadn’t been sealed and there were no warning notices posted on the front door, alerting neighbours.
While the business in question had been registered as a company, the operator had not registered with the department of agriculture, land reform and rural development, as required by law, so did not have a required “P number”.

• All registration holders of aluminium phosphide-containing fumigants have committed to ensuring that their products are only sold to licensed people, that those licensed only sell their products to bona fide farmers and registered pest control operators, and that full sales records are recorded in poison registers, as demanded by law.
• Registration holders of aluminium phosphide-containing products will, of their own accord, notify distributors and retailers to whom they supply the products, telling them not to sell them on to other distributors or retailers who are not licensed.
• The industry will report all unlawful conduct with aluminium phosphide to the registrar and the chief of the inspectorate of the Directorate of Agricultural Inputs Control, the department of health and to the SAPS, with the charges spelt out in terms of the Act and regulations.
• The industry calls on the department of health to increase its inspection of retail outlets to ensure they comply with requirements.
• Members of the public must verify any company or individual who offers pest control services is registered with a valid pest control operator certificate (not a training certificate). And if fumigation is to be done by such a registered pest control operator, the person must have that specific competence listed on their pest control operator registration certificate.
According to Moses Chetty vice-president of the Pest Control Federation of South Africa: This substance should never be used inside. Any fumigation has a period where everyone must be evacuated for 18-24 hours/ minimum two days and two nights. “You cannot fumigate a single unit in a block of flats using a fumigant unless the entire block is evacuated. That is a standard rule for a fumigation. We fumigate where the block is sealed, using a tent. The fumigation period is 18–24 hours – the evacuation period is a minimum of two days and two nights,” said Chetty, a qualified fumigator who has been in the pest-control business since 1982. Fumigation differs from pest control which is targeted at removing general pests like cockroaches, rats and fish moths.
“In pest control, a pesticide spray is applied,” said Chetty. He added that alternate measures are considered prior to fumigation. “We look at alternatives: Can we implement removal and replacement if there is one board or panel affected by wood borer, for example? Another option is palliative treatment where we carry out spot treatment to the affected areas by drilling and injecting them with an approved wood preservative,” he explained.
The qualification process for fumigation professionals
Chetty noted several changes in the current qualification process for fumigation professionals.
“In my day, we attended an academic correspondence course that included six subjects and several examinations. Once we completed academic training, we would work under a qualified pest controller who would then sign us off. We then needed to make an application to the Department of Agriculture to become a registered pest-control operator. These days, the process has become simplified with a three-day training course, followed by a six-month work period with a qualified pest-control operator who will write a letter of motivation for the student to apply to the department. What can you learn in three days?” asked Chetty.
However, the real issue, for Chetty, is fraudulent permits.
“The danger I see is that a student can sit in the three-day training without really taking in the knowledge and then find a registered pest-control operator who will accept a fee to write a motivation letter without the six-month period needed,” said Chetty.
How to verify a registered fumigation service:
Chetty called on consumers to verify pest-control companies online by visiting the South African Pest Control Association website, https://sapca.org.za or the Pest Control Federation of South Africa website, https://pcfsa.co.za
PAST CASES OF THIS TYPE OF POISONING: Two weeks BEFORE this couple, a two-year-old died after a family used the same substance for indoor fumigation, and about a year ago, a family in the Free State bought the product for indoor fumigation which resulted in the deaths of children and adults in the family. Dr Verdoorn was called in both those cases and can talk about them.

Fumigation Script 7 for FRIDAY VIEWING

Matri pronounced MaTREE

1. V/O
This is Observatory Court in Durban, the flat where Zoe Molver was born nearly 70 years ago...

UPS CHAT FROM KITCHEN

2. V/O
It’s a place that holds precious memories…where Zoe's three boys were looked after by their grandparents here, while she was at work…

Her sons had such a unique bond that when they flew the nest, they all gravitated back to the familiar embrace of the block of flats that provided them with a sense of certainty and comfort.

Zoe
It is a flat of hope and a flat of joy and a flat of great history.

3. V/O
When Zoe’s mother died, her middle son Nicholas and his wife Matri moved into what had been their grandparents’ home - flat number 31.

Zoe
They were at the start of a new life.

4. V/O
The couple were about to celebrate their fourth wedding anniversary.
Matri was a gifted graphic designer with a great job and Nicholas, a communication officer for an NGO. Everything changed on the 27th of September 2022.

Link
It was an ordinary Tuesday night Nicholas and Matri Molver were here in their flat doing some work. They had a glass of wine each, showered and then went to bed, but they never woke up again.

4b V/O
When the cleaning service couldn’t get into their flat that morning, the caretaker asked Nicholas’ older brother, Luke, who had a key, to let them in.

Luke
I called them names. I walked around the bed called their names. I saw their faces were blue and I touched my brother’s face, and he was cold. And I knew immediately.

Zoe
And the caretaker phoned and she said Zoe you better come now, and in the background, I could hear my Matthew and my Luke howling.

5. V/O
It is the call that every parent dreads…

Up Sound Car?

Zoe
I stopped the car and I could see the courtyard was filled with cops and I got out and Luke came up to me and said Mom, Nick is dead and Matri is dead.

Masa
I am so sorry

Zoe
Because the thing with loss is that you will never see them again.

Fade down

Fade up

5a V/O
Nicholas and Matri lived at the end of the second floor in flat number 31 and shared a common wall with flat number 32 where a fumigation had taken place.

Luke
There was, although I did not initially notice it, I think probably because I was just in this state there was a distinct smell of toxic gas and the fire department was called in. They determined that the gas was not coming from within my brother and sister’s flat but the flat next door had been fumigated.



Link
In this flat, rogue fumigators threw aluminium phosphide pellets all over the place. Now when the pellets come into contact with moisture from the air, they start to release a gas which is colourless, flammable and deadly.

Moses
Fumigation is dangerous. It’s not dangerous if you know what you are doing. In this case, it became dangerous because the individual didn’t even know what he was playing with.

6. V/O
The police roped in Moses Chetty, vice president of the Pest Control Federation of South Africa… who’s been in the business for forty years. He recorded his assessment on his cell phone.

UPS
These tablets are all over the show here. This is an overkill. This is not pest control practice. This is beyond comprehension. This is suicidal.


7 . V/O
The fumigation industry in Durban is thriving… and it’s because of pests like these: wood-eating ants and borer beetles…
Before a home can be sold it’s sealed up… or tented… and flooded with toxic gas, to kill the insects living in the wood.

Observatory Court is no exception… Luke’s own flat is damaged where wood borer ate through the skirtings and floorboards.




Luke
The floors in the fumigated flat. And the floors in this flat are wooden. And there's a space between them. And as in Durban, everything's riddled with woodworm. So I think that is one part of the one aspect of how the get into the flats.

Moses
The doors were not sealed and the windows were not sealed and the wind was blowing everything into this passage.

8. V/O
And under the door of Nicholas and Matri’s flat.

Zoe
Well, Nicholas and Matri died in a place that everybody would regard as safe. They died in the bedroom as a result of the reckless negligence of strangers.

9. V/O
Zoe believes that those “strangers” need to be held accountable.

9b. V/O
She and her sons have tracked the events… to support the police investigation, putting together a dossier of their evidence.

Zoe
The caretaker noted on her CCTV that two men were walking through the courtyard. She went out and asked what they needed, who they were, and they announced that they were Mr. Khan, the fumigate and a helper, and they were there to remove a stove from the flat number 32.

10. V/O
The flat was unoccupied at the time and had borer damage.
The owner hired KZN FUMIGATORS…a newly-established company. The owner: Irshaad Khan was paid ten thousand rands to remove the stove and fumigate.

The owner had not informed anyone of the fumigation and Khan only mentioned it by chance… when the caretaker saw them leaving.

Zoe
And she said, well, do I need to tell the young couple. And they said, Mr. Khan said, No, it will be done. Will we be finished? It's not anything to worry about.

11. V/O
Pest Control Regulations are strict on fumigation. The tenants should have been informed… the flats evacuated. Fumigation display boards should have been placed in prominent positions. None of this happened.

Dr Gerhard Verdoon, one of South Africa’s top experts on pesticides believed that if Irshaad Khan had just read the label he would have seen it was the wrong product to use.

Gerhard
But there is no reason to think it can be safely applied in any premises where people work or reside because where people work in hospitality whatever. It was never intended for that purpose. It is not on any label of any aluminium phosphide in the country that it can be used in a domestic situation.

Moses
Mr Khan is not even a pest control operator, he is a normal, a normal citizen who is taking a chance and tried his luck.

12. V/O
Mntu Mbhele…a retired Hawks captain, now in private security …believes Khan’s actions were criminal.

Mntu
The first thing that came to my mind, if this is not investigated this can go on and happen elsewhere.

13. V/O
Mbhele has been assisting the police in their investigations, and what he has uncovered is startling.

Mntu
Whoever was the company they didn’t have a licence and digging more I realised that even the licence used did not belong to the people fumigating.




14. V/O
The evidence indicates that Khan wasn’t registered as a pest control operator and he used a deadly chemical in a residential setting… to buy the aluminium phosphide, he fraudulently used a licence that did not belong to him.

When he bought the poison from a wholesale company he said his intended use was for mole control.

Link
Aluminium phosphide can only be purchased and used by a registered fumigator, but we have been doing our own research and anyone can buy it online. And some companies will even courier it to your home.

15. V/O
We called two South African companies and asked them whether they knew it was illegal to sell the product to unlicensed users.

Masa
It’s a toxic chemical that is not allowed to be sold.

Debbie
We buy it freely from our supplier, they have never, never ever mentioned to us that it is that toxic that it kills people, and if this is what you are telling me I will never ever ever sell it again. God Forbid.

De Klerk
We have seen that there is a possible issue with this. We stopped the sales, we stopped the transportation and all stock has been uplifted and returned to the supplier.

16. V/O
True to their word, an hour after our phone calls to the companies the aluminium phosphide products were no longer available on their websites.

But what about holding Irshaad Khan accountable?

Up Sound Hi there how are you?


17. V/O
He was not at home, his mother spoke to us, but did not want to appear on camera.

Mother
You are misinformed.

Masa
No, I am not. You are misinformed. You are biased because you are his mother. What I am working with is facts.

Masa
What I am saying to you is when somebody uses somebody else’s licence and buys a toxic substance, it is fraud and then takes that toxic substance and uses it for fumigation in a residential area that is not supposed to be used. That is illegal.

Mother
I am waiting for the lawyer to come back to us. He is not running away. Obviously he is devastated and wants closure on this matter.

18. V/O
Believing that justice delayed is justice denied. The family sent the deceased’s biological samples for private testing. It’s reported that there’s an up to 8 years backlog on state toxicology results. The Molver’s weren’t prepared to wait that long.

19. V/O
I was finally able to speak to Irshaad Khan.

Irshaad
I am not allowed to talk to any news reporters or news channels

Masa
But you are also not allowed to use aluminium phosphide in a residential area and yet you did

Irshaad
Yes, I am not allowed to talk to you. Listen, I have got the police on my case. I have got them handling, dealing with my lawyers….I am stressed out.

Masa
You are stressed out. Zoe Molver has lost her son and daughter in law and you want to tell me you are stressed out. You are stressed out when you use a toxic illegal gas . Oh there he goes. He says he’s stressed out.

20 V/O
The private laboratory completed the toxicology tests within a week and it confirmed aluminium phosphide poisoning… which could make arrests possible.

Link
One of the things that this tragedy has highlighted is that if you are going to hire someone to work with dangerous chemicals in your home, you need to make sure that they are registered with the relevant authorities. You can’t rely on the fact that they are the experts and know what they are doing?

Moses
Consumers must catch a wake up, you make the wrong choices and this is what can happen.
Why do you want to deal with an unknown entity. You don’t even check his credentials.

Zoe
I squarely blame Mr Irshaad Khan and the owner of No 32. Both are capable.
It is not good enough that people can behave so recklessly and negligently and my two children die needlessly.

Programme End

V/O When Zoe’s mother died, her middle son Nicholas and his wife Matri moved into what had been their grandparents’ home - flat number 31. Zoe They were at the start of a new life. 4. V/O The couple were about to celebrate their fourth wedding anniversary. Matri was a gifted graphic designer with a great job and Nicholas, a communication officer for an NGO. Everything changed on the 27th of September 2022. Link It was an ordinary Tuesday night Nicholas and Matri Molver were here in their flat doing some work. Zoe And the caretaker phoned and she said Zoe you better come now, and in the background, I could hear my Matthew and my Luke howling. 5. V/O It is the call that every parent dreads… Up Sound Car? Luke There was, although I did not initially notice it, I think probably because I was just in this state there was a distinct smell of toxic gas and the fire department was called in. Moses Mr Khan is not even a pest control operator, he is a normal, a normal citizen who is taking a chance and tried his luck. 12. Mntu The first thing that came to my mind, if this is not investigated this can go on and happen elsewhere. 13.
